newsitem.title: MEXICO: Drugs linked to Mexican assassination - report. [CORRECTED 22:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Drugs linked to Mexican assassination - report. [CORRECTED 22:40 GMT]

text.p: Drug traffickers appear linked to two high-level criminal cases in Mexico, a newspaper reported on Sunday.
(Corrects headline and text to show that one, not both of the cases involved an assassination.)
Mexico City's daily El Financiero reported the link of drug dealers in the March 1994 assassination of Mexican presidential candidate Luis Donaldo Colosio.
"We can't count out that narco traffickers are involved (in the Colosio murder)," El Financiero quoted the special prosecutor in the case, Luis Raul Gonzalez Perez, as saying.

The Swiss government also said two days ago it suspected drug money flowed into the accounts of Raul Salinas de Gortari, the brother of former President Carlos Salinas de Gortari. Raul Salinas was arrested for killing Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu, secretary general of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) in 1995.
The recent disclosures add to increasing anecdotal evidence that the Colosio assassination and case of Raul Salinas were both intertwined with the drug trade.
U.S. officials say international drug cartels spend $6 billion a year bribing Mexican officials for safe passage of their illicit product to the lucrative U.S. market.

Colosio was gunned down at a campaign rally in the northern border city of Tijuana on March 23, 1994. So far only one man, confessed gunman Mario Aburto, has been definitively linked to the crime after four special prosecutors have probed 27 lines of investigation.
According to the El Financiero report, investigators have established that Colosio had contacts with the Juarez-based Gulf cartel.

Colosio was also forced to cancel the party invitation of Humberto Garcia Abrego, brother and lieutenant of Juan Garcia Abrego, the one-time chief of the Gulf cartel. Juan Garcia Abrego was caught in 1996 and deported to the United States, where he was sentenced to life in prison by a federal court.

According to one unproven theory, the Tijuana-based Pacific drug cartel may have wanted Colosio dead for fear that he was too close to the rival Gulf cartel and might side with them in order to crack down on Tijuana.
"We have to investigate whether the policies that Luis Donaldo Colosio was trying to implement could have affected certain drug cartels," Gonzalez, the special prosecutor, said.

In the second case, PRI secretary general Ruiz Massieu was shot and killed outside a Mexico City hotel on September 28, 1994. In Feburary 1995, Raul Salinas was arrested on suspicion of ordering the murder.

After Raul Salinas was jailed, his wife was caught attempting to withdraw money from a secret Swiss bank account that her husband controlled under an assumed name. The Swiss government since has frozen $84 million of Raul Salinas's money pending an investigation.
Raul Salinas was questioned by Swiss prosecutors last week. He claimed the money came from an investment scheme involving some of Mexico's richest men.
